algorithm1_implements_F_D_tau.evidence_authority: algorithm-specification.md §11 Algorithm 1 procedure; appendix-c C.2.0.1 and C.8.1
algorithm1_implements_F_D_tau.evidence: Algorithm 1 explicitly composes resolution (lines 9–31) with classification (lines 32–36) and aggregation (line 37). The header declares the output signature F_{D,tau} in bold; no line reduces the procedure to a call on the ideal E.

algorithm1_not_reduced_to_ideal_f.evidence: The procedure never invokes f(E). It resolves observations through validation, freshness, exclusion, kappa derivation and solar lookup, then evaluates five component classifiers and aggregates. f(E) shorthand is never used in the pseudocode.

startup_v_semantics_preserved.evidence: Lines 1–3 refuse startup when v not in V and return a STARTUP_CONFIGURATION_ERROR. Postcondition Q2 states 'This is not a runtime observation fault.' No line ever returns UNSAFE for missing v.

D_wellformedness_preserved.evidence: Repaired 2026-09-10 by the Exclusion-Set Domain Repair. Line 5 now tests 't in D' or 'D not subset of C = {w,r,m,o,t}' and refuses startup on either; (D2) D strict subset of C follows automatically from (D1) since t in C \ D. The check is expressed against C rather than against a narrowed universe. The maximal well-formed exclusion set D = {w,r,m,o} is admitted (appendix-c C.2.0.5, 'Why this lemma matters more than it looks'). The earlier wording additionally rejected D = {w,r,m,o}, which was stronger than canonical and has been removed.

exclusion_maximal_wellformed_D_admitted.evidence_authority: algorithm-specification.md §11 lines 4–8; §12 P4 (final sentence); §15 boundary case B25; appendix-c C.2.0.5
exclusion_maximal_wellformed_D_admitted.evidence: D = {w,r,m,o} satisfies (D1) t not in D and (D2) D strict subset of C = {w,r,m,o,t} since t in C \ D.
